annotationRationale: The key is identifying the favorable event in a uniform assignment without replacement. The two routes then use conditional multiplication or combination counting.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct. No area repair is proposed.

review.questionCheck: The captains are the three tallest exactly when those athletes receive different colors. Uniform drawing without replacement gives probability (6/8)(3/7)=9/28, agreeing with choice C and the key. No statement or choice contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Independently checked and retained both shared methods from 2025_AMC_10B_Q14: sequential-band-draws and unordered-band-sample. They provide distinct conditional-probability and unordered-counting explanations. The current LIVE and Random Math references use the sequential route; no further route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Assessed cnm_h137 appropriately captures the equally likely probability model; support cnm_310 captures sampling without replacement. The two methods supply their precise conditional-multiplication and combination concepts. No contextual node is needed.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct. No area repair is proposed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The different-colors condition is proved in both directions. Uniform assignments justify treating the tallest three as drawing first. The second athlete has six acceptable bands among eight; conditional on success, the third has three among seven. Their product is 9/28.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly credits 2025_AMC_10B_Q14#sequential-band-draws and retains both inherited LIVE and Random Math reference IDs. The explanation agrees with the supplied project method and current references. Project reuse and source-informed-original status are explicit; no official MAA authorship is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation motivates focusing on the tallest three, justifies reordering the draws, and makes the conditioning explicit. Every decisive transition is reconstructible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h137, cnm_h245, and cnm_310 directly match uniform outcome ratios, ordered conditional multiplication, and sampling without replacement.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact classical-probability and without-replacement links fit. The partial multiplication-rule link also fits: all conditioning events here have positive probability.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: S-CP.B.8 fits conditional multiplication in this uniform model, and 7.SP.C.8a fits compound-outcome fractions. This route does not demonstrate the permutation/combination computation of S-CP.B.9. cnm_310 has no supplied US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three immediate nodes are supported by the written derivation; no broader substitute or additional problem-specific node is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Labeling bands yields 84 equally likely three-band subsets, each with the same assignment multiplicity. Favorable subsets choose one band of each color, giving 3^3=27. Thus 27/84=9/28. The event equivalence and absence of overcounting are justified.
